name: SelectableCard
description: A Card that is one selectable option; grouped into single (radio) or multiple (checkbox) sets via SelectableCardGroup.

keyboard: Tab moves focus into the group
Arrow keys move within a single-select set (native radio)
ariaRequirements: Group renders a fieldset with a legend for the accessible name
Each card is a label wrapping a native radio/checkbox input
Error announces via role=alert and sets aria-invalid on the group
a11y.reviewedNote: 2026-07-12 — alpha→beta: code-level a11y review. SelectableCardGroup renders a fieldset with a legend for the accessible name; each SelectableCard is a label wrapping a visually-hidden native radio (single) or checkbox (multiple) input, so keyboard, focus and form submission come from the platform. Error announces via role=alert and sets aria-invalid on the group. Selected/disabled states mirror to data-attributes for CSS + tests. Motion respects prefers-reduced-motion. Axe asserted in the colocated a11y test; forced-colors + light/dark verified on a non-6010 Storybook. 2026-10-15: promoted to stable. Production consumers per audit:consumers; evidence recaptured in light, dark and forced-colors (real Chromium forced-colors pass) against 1b3b7d94a, every record passing with axe clean.

disabled.description: Per-card disable; the choice stays visible.

selected.description: Standalone selected state when used outside a SelectableCardGroup.

onSelectedChange.description: Standalone change handler when used outside a SelectableCardGroup.

forbiddenUse: nest interactive controls (buttons, links) inside a SelectableCard; the whole card is a label wrapping the input, so nested controls steal the click. Use a plain Card for action cards.
use it for navigation; selecting must not commit or route on click.
dense: Card as one selectable option; grouped via SelectableCardGroup into single (radio) or multiple (checkbox) sets; whole card is a label over a hidden native input; controlled or uncontrolled.

usage.description: Use SelectableCardGroup for visually prominent form choices, with SelectableCard children representing radio-style exclusive options or checkbox-style multiple options. The group owns the legend, value state, and error relationship.

bestPractices.description: Write the group legend as the question and keep each card title short and scannable.
Use single selection for a few rich exclusive options and multiple selection for independent add-ons.
For one standalone toggle outside a group, control selected and onSelectedChange directly.
Do not nest buttons or links inside a selectable card; use Card for action-oriented content.
For bare text options without supporting content, use RadioGroup or CheckboxGroup.
